Theme 085 · Art movements & eras

Constructivist Agitprop

Soviet avant-garde poster grammar — El Lissitzky's wedge, Rodchenko's megaphone, hard diagonals and shouting uppercase — re-inked in Acme teal and coral on cream. The film argues like a 1920s poster: the teal wedge pierces the circle of blind spots, the megaphone shouts the anomaly, and the call to action is a literal slogan.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Wedge — teal triangle that pierces the circle — Pulse cutting through blind spots
  • Diagonal bands — ink/coral/teal bars at −27°…+4° that carry mono captions
  • Megaphone cone — coral trapezoid emanating from the Acme mark; the anomaly is shouted in it
  • Slogan type — Manrope 800 uppercase, −0.04em tracking, rotated −4…−8°
  • Shards — small rectangles scattered on impact frames
  • Slogan button — rotated block CTA with a ▶ glyph

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Slash-in — bands translate along their own angle from off-frame, expo.out 0.35 s, landing on 8th-note offbeats
  • Wedge strike — wedge x from +700 px to 0, power4.in 0.25 s, impact exactly on the drop; 2-frame camera shake ±6 px
  • Megaphone unfold — cone scaleX 0→1 from its narrow end, back.out(1.4) 0.5 s = one beat, text scales 1.15→1 on the next downbeat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Constructivism was designed to make a single message impossible to miss, which is exactly what an anomaly alert needs; the diagonals give built-in motion vectors for every cut. Risk: the political baggage — keep it about form (wedge, megaphone, diagonals), avoid stars, sickles or propaganda slogans.

Adapt to your product: Make the wedge your product and the circle the problem it breaks; put your key alert or feature result inside the megaphone. Your CTA becomes the slogan on the final band.
